mem.7:
Caroline (surname unknown) and Melanie (“Mel,” surname unknown) are friends who kept in touch in 2023. Caroline is transgender; she began transitioning around 2020 and had been transitioning for three years by 9 June 2023. She moved from her home country around 2019 and has supportive friends, family, and mentors. Melanie is married with children.

**8 May 2023:** Melanie was busy with work and children. Caroline had attended an LGBTQ support group on 7 May; hearing others’ stories helped her feel accepted and more courageous about embracing herself. She planned to continue her education and explore counseling/mental-health work supporting people with similar experiences. Melanie said Caroline’s empathy would make her a good counselor. Caroline shared a photo of a dog by a wall painting of a woman; Melanie liked the painting. Melanie shared her 2022 sunrise-over-a-lake painting, which she made to express feelings, be creative, and relax. Caroline praised its colors and agreed art helps with relaxation and self-expression. Melanie went swimming with her children.

**25 May 2023:** Melanie had run a mental-health charity race on 20 May. She was trying to make time for running, reading, or violin; self-care was a work in progress, and looking after herself helped her care for her family. Her children anticipated summer break; the family was considering June camping. Caroline was researching adoption agencies and shared a photo of an agency sign/building. Having a family and giving children in need a loving home had long been her dream. She chose an agency supportive of LGBTQ+ adopters and planned to become a single adoptive parent. She was hopeful and excited but aware of the challenges. Melanie encouraged her and said she’d be an awesome mom.

**9 June 2023:** Caroline described speaking at a school event the previous week about her transgender journey, personal struggles, coming out, and growth. Audience members related and were inspired to become better allies. She believes conversations about gender identity and inclusion are necessary; sharing stories can promote understanding, acceptance, and hope. Having received love and support, she wanted to use her voice to support the trans community and build community. Melanie praised her courage and advocacy; they hoped to motivate and support each other.

Melanie said her husband and children motivate her and give her love; she wanted to be courageous for her family. Caroline called friends, family, and mentors her “rocks.” She shared a photo of a group posing in a yard: supportive friends she’d known for four years, since moving from her home country around 2019; they helped especially after a difficult breakup. Melanie shared photos of her husband and a little girl by a waterfall, her wedding (herself in a dress with a bouquet), and a family picnic (a man and woman on a blanket eating). She and her husband had been married five years, since around 2018. Family outings with games and good food made her feel happy and alive; Caroline said time with loved ones brings happiness and gratitude.

**27 June 2023:** Caroline shared a photo of a necklace with a cross and heart, given by her grandmother in Sweden when Caroline was young. It represents love, faith, strength, roots, and family support. Asked about treasured objects, Caroline said a friend made her a hand-painted bowl for her 18th birthday, about ten years earlier; its pattern and colors remind her of art and self-expression. Melanie showed patterned bowls. Melanie’s family had camped in the mountains around 19–25 June: nature, marshmallows, hikes, and an amazing summit view; her two younger children love nature.

Caroline shared a bookshelf photo while considering counseling/mental-health work, possibly with trans people. On 23 June she attended an LGBTQ+ counseling workshop about therapeutic methods and working effectively with trans people; she was moved by professionals’ commitment to safe spaces. Her own journey and counseling/support groups helped her understand and accept herself; she wanted to offer others a safe, inviting place to grow. Melanie encouraged her and shared a bookshelf-in-a-room photo.

**3 July 2023:** Caroline had attended an LGBTQ+ pride parade the previous week (26 June–2 July); the happy crowd made her feel she belonged and showed how much the community had grown. It motivated her to help others; she was leaning toward counseling/mental-health work. She looked forward to a transgender conference in July to meet people and learn about advocacy; Melanie wished her a safe, fun trip and Caroline promised updates. Melanie had signed up for pottery the previous day, finding clay calming, therapeutic, creative, and expressive. She shared a photo of someone holding a frisbee and a black-and-white flower-design bowl she made; she was proud of the work and said pottery was a major part of her life, not just a hobby. Caroline was learning piano and admired the bowl.

**6 July 2023, 8:18 p.m.:** Caroline said counseling/mental-health work felt challenging but rewarding and aligned with her wish to help people. Melanie had taken her children to a museum on 5 July and shared a photo of two children in a water-play area. They loved the dinosaur exhibit, especially the bones, reminding Melanie why she loved being a mom. Caroline shared a photo of a bookcase filled with books and toys for her future children: children’s classics, stories from different cultures, and educational books. Melanie’s favorite childhood book was *Charlotte’s Web*, for its friendship and compassion; she shared its cover (girl and cat). Caroline said friends and family had given her love, guidance, and acceptance through her transition, helping her accept and grow into her true self. She shared a photo of women on a park picnic blanket from the previous week. Melanie shared her family camping by a beach campfire; camping brings them closer.

**12 July 2023:** Caroline said she had attended an LGBTQ conference on 10 July, where meeting people with similar journeys and feeling accepted strengthened her gratitude for the community and resolve to fight for trans rights and awareness. She was still exploring counseling/mental-health jobs because her own mental-health struggles and helpful support made her want to help others find support systems. Melanie encouraged her. Melanie shared a photo of a book cover with a gold coin, saying a book she read in 2022 reminded her to pursue dreams. Caroline said books guide and motivate her; her favorite was *Becoming Nicole* by Amy Ellis Nutt, a true story about a trans girl and her family that gave her connection and hope. She took from it self-acceptance, finding support, and the idea that tough times don’t last; hope and love exist. She also noted pets bring joy.

Melanie shared a photo of two little girls on steps with a dog, then a cat lying on the floor. Her family has a dog and cat named Luna and Oliver; they are sweet and playful. She shared photos of pink/purple running shoes and said she had been running farther to destress and improve her headspace/mental health. Caroline encouraged her to keep it up and prioritize self-care.

Caroline (surname unknown) and Melanie (“Mel,” surname unknown) are friends who stayed in touch in 2023. Friends and family have supported her with love, guidance and acceptance; she calls them her “rocks,” and their support helped her accept and grow into her true self. Family is everything to Caroline, and time with loved ones brings happiness and gratitude. Melanie is married with children; her family motivates her, and she cherishes family time and feels alive and happy with them. Her family also helped her through a move and tough times. Melanie is learning self-care: it’s a work in progress, but caring for herself helps her care for her family.

8 May 2023: Caroline attended an LGBTQ support group on 7 May; hearing others’ stories helped her feel accepted and confident. She planned further education and to explore counseling/mental-health work; Melanie thought she’d make a good counselor. Melanie was busy with work and children. They discussed Melanie’s 2022 sunrise-over-lake painting, made for expression and relaxation, a dog beside a wall painting, and swimming with her children.

25 May: Melanie ran a mental-health charity race on 20 May and tried to make time for running, reading or violin. Her children anticipated summer break; family considered June camping. Caroline researched adoption agencies and shared a photo. She dreamed of parenting and giving a child in need a loving home, chose an agency supportive of LGBTQ+ adopters, and planned to adopt as a single parent. Hopeful but aware of challenges, she was encouraged by Melanie, who said she’d be a great mom.

9 June: Caroline spoke at a school about her trans journey, struggles, coming out and growth; audience members related and were inspired to be better allies. She wants to advocate for trans people and believes stories foster understanding, acceptance and hope. A photo showed friends she’d known four years, since moving around 2019; they supported her especially after a difficult breakup. Melanie shared wedding, family and outing photos. She and her husband had been married five years (since about 2018); games and good food on outings make her happy.

27 June: Caroline’s grandmother in Sweden gave her a cross-and-heart necklace when she was young; it represents love, faith, strength, roots and family support. A friend made her a hand-painted bowl for her 18th birthday, about ten years earlier; its colors/pattern evoke art and self-expression. Melanie showed patterned bowls. Her family camped in the mountains around 19–25 June, enjoying nature, hikes, marshmallows and summit views; her two younger children love nature. The family also likes beach camping. Caroline attended an LGBTQ+ counseling workshop on 23 June, encouraging her to consider counseling, perhaps with trans people. Support groups and her journey helped her accept herself. They shared bookshelf photos.

3–15 July: Caroline attended a pride parade during 26 June–2 July; she felt accepted, happy, proud and grateful among people celebrating her, and it inspired her to help others. She planned to attend a transgender conference in July to meet community members and learn advocacy; she attended an LGBTQ conference on 10 July, strengthening her resolve to advocate for trans rights and awareness. She explored mental-health jobs, learned piano, and her favorite book is Amy Ellis Nutt’s *Becoming Nicole*, an inspiring true story about a trans girl and her family that made her feel connected and hopeful. She built a library for future children with classic, diverse and educational books; Melanie’s childhood favorite was *Charlotte’s Web*. Caroline’s favorite color is blue, which relaxes her; sunflowers suggest warmth/happiness and roses love/beauty. Melanie signed up for pottery on 2 July, finding it calming and expressive; she made a black-and-white flower-design bowl and felt proud, plus other colorful pottery. She took her children to a museum on 5 July; they loved dinosaur bones. Her pets are Luna (dog) and Oliver (cat); running farther helps her destress. On the weekend of 8–9 July, Melanie and her children painted a sunset and palm tree together, chatting about nature; they finished another similar painting by 17 July. They also made pots, including a dog-face cup, and enjoyed purple flowers. Caroline attended an adoption council meeting that Friday, strengthening her resolve. Flowers remind Melanie of growth, beauty, small moments and her wedding; marrying her partner and promising to stay together forever was her favorite part. Caroline said being herself without fear was the best part of transition. Melanie’s family camped in a forest. Caroline had a picnic with friends during the week before 6 July.

17–20 July: Melanie had a quiet, unplugged weekend after family camping 1–2 July. Caroline mentored a transgender teen through an LGBTQ youth mentorship program; seeing her mentee feel supported at a June pride event was especially meaningful. She planned an LGBTQ art show for August. A preview painting of a tree and bright sun represented unity and strength. On 18 July she joined Connected LGBTQ Activists, a group that plans events/campaigns and supports members. She missed her city’s pride parade the prior weekend, but marchers, flags and signs reminded her change is possible and people aren’t alone. Melanie’s family went to the beach; the children flew a kite. They enjoy camping, marshmallows and campfire stories. Melanie treasured seeing the Perseid meteor shower on a camping trip the previous year and her youngest child’s first steps. Photos included a baby in a white crib with blue blanket and family at a beach sunset.

14–17 August: Melanie celebrated her daughter’s birthday the previous night at a Matt Patterson concert. Caroline attended an advocacy event and a pride parade on 11 August; its energy, love and diversity reinforced equality and LGBTQ rights. Melanie shared an “all are welcome” sign and event photos, saying inclusion matters for their children. Caroline uses art to represent inclusivity/diversity and promote LGBTQ+ acceptance. Her painting “Embracing Identity” shows a woman in a red shirt and represents comfort, love, acceptance, warmth and self-love. On 17 August Caroline said a hike had gone badly after religious conservatives said something upsetting; it reminded her LGBTQ rights still need work. Supportive people reassure her she’ll be okay. Melanie showed an eye-catching colorful patterned pottery bowl; art is a learning experience, sanctuary, comfort and way to express feelings. Both valued happy moments and their friendship. They recalled enjoying Pride fest with friends the previous year (photo of people on a street with balloons) and planned a special outing together that summer, possibly in nature.

23 August: Caroline applied to adoption agencies after getting help at an adoption advice/assistance group; excited but nervous about parenting responsibility. She has a guinea pig named Oscar; a photo showed him eating parsley, his favorite vegetable. Melanie had added a cat named Bailey; pets are doing well. Oliver once hid his bone in Melanie’s slipper. Melanie had fed a horse a carrot and painted a horse on a wooden wall; she enjoys painting animals for their grace and peace. Caroline rode horses through fields with her father as a child and has always loved horses. She shared a blue-faced self-portrait painted the previous week; painting made her feel liberated and empowered, helping explore identity and be true to herself. Art, supportive people, LGBTQ rights work and authenticity give Caroline freedom; she wants to help others live authentically. Melanie congratulated and supported her adoption journey.
